methodology: Qualitative fits grounded in the catalog's source summaries, methods and dependencies, not measured rankings. Exact skill IDs link recommendations to source evidence. Contexts suggest small complementary stacks, not installation requirements; they neither hide other stage skills nor override user choices. Use each skill's setup and approval gates.

contexts.label: New app idea
contexts.reason: Use this when the product direction is still rough and framework choices need current evidence.

picks.reason: Converges candidate ideas into MVP scope, exclusions and validation questions.
Produces a cited note from official documentation, source and specifications.

contexts.label: Unfamiliar existing app
contexts.reason: Use this when a requested change needs both an accurate goal and a source-grounded system map.

picks.reason: Restates the user's goal before solving the wrong problem.
Explains architecture and runtime flow from source, scaling exploration to scope.

contexts.label: Single app feature
contexts.reason: Use this when a feature needs an approved specification followed by small, verifiable implementation tasks.

picks.reason: Defines objectives, commands, tests and boundaries, then stops for later human approval.
Turns the approved specification into vertical slices with acceptance criteria and verification commands.

contexts.label: Tracker backed delivery
contexts.reason: Use this with Matt's tracker setup when an existing design conversation must become an executable ticket graph.

picks.reason: Synthesizes existing decisions into a specification and confirms high test seams.
Publishes user-approved tracer-bullet tickets with explicit blocking edges.

contexts.label: Reviewed multi-service design
contexts.reason: Use this after design review when the team already uses Linear and Akash's ownership conventions.

picks.reason: Sequences shared foundations before disjoint tasks with owned paths, contracts and tests.

contexts.label: App module boundaries
contexts.reason: Use this when internal modules and their exposed contracts need clear, testable boundaries.

picks.reason: Designs deep modules with small interfaces and deliberate test seams.
Specifies boundary parsing, consistent errors, compatibility and safe idempotency behavior.

contexts.label: Uncertain interaction design
contexts.reason: Use this when a UI decision needs a disposable interactive demonstration rather than production implementation.

picks.reason: Tests a design question with a shareable state demo or multiple UI variants.

contexts.label: Reviewed multi-service PRD
contexts.reason: Use this with Akash's design conventions to move sequentially from reviewed product requirements to service details.

picks.reason: Assigns responsibilities and interactions while deferring implementation internals.
Expands reviewed high-level design into contracts, schemas, state machines and test seams.

contexts.label: Existing multi-service app
contexts.reason: Use this for incremental feature work in an existing app that already follows Akash's service conventions.

picks.reason: Delivers usable vertical slices with verification, green builds and safe feature flags.
Separates API, domain and database models while enforcing typed boundaries and injected dependencies.

contexts.label: Solo UI feature
contexts.reason: Use this for a single developer adding a user-facing feature without a parallel-worker workflow.

picks.reason: Implements, tests and verifies one usable slice at a time.
Adds intentional layout, accessible interactions and loading, empty and error states.

contexts.label: Parallel ticket delivery
contexts.reason: Use this with Matt's tracker setup and a ready ticket graph when independent work can use separate worktrees.

picks.reason: Runs ready ticket frontiers in separate worktrees, merges results and reviews integration.
Separates owned files, branches or keys before introducing shared-state locks.

contexts.label: Lightweight typed code
contexts.reason: Use this for a bounded TypeScript change that needs explicit type discipline without a broad orchestration workflow.

picks.reason: Uses discriminated unions, validated brands, schema-derived types and exhaustive narrowing.
Verifies each work unit before proceeding and orders commits around executable evidence.

contexts.label: Browser feature change
contexts.reason: Use this when behavior needs both failing-test proof and evidence from the running browser.

picks.reason: Uses actual repository commands and red-green-refactor to prove behavior changes.
Captures DOM, console, network and accessibility evidence in an isolated browser profile.

contexts.label: Unexplained app failure
contexts.reason: Use this when debugging needs a discriminating executable signal before any proposed fix.

picks.reason: Proves a failing signal, ranks hypotheses and instruments one prediction at a time.
Checks the real output rather than relying on proxies or worker self-reports.

contexts.label: Measured performance change
contexts.reason: Use this when a suspected user-visible bottleneck needs profiling and a defensible before-and-after comparison.

picks.reason: Profiles one measured bottleneck and keeps or reverts targeted changes after remeasurement.
Checks harness fairness, machine load, repeated trials, errors and end-to-end relevance.

contexts.label: Routine feature diff
contexts.reason: Use this for a bounded change that needs a general quality review without multiple broad review workflows.

picks.reason: Assesses correctness, readability, architecture, security and performance against context and evidence.

contexts.label: Exposed trust boundary
contexts.reason: Use this when a small-looking change touches external inputs, authorization or another consequential safety assumption.

picks.reason: Maps assets and trust boundaries, then checks authorization, secrets and destructive paths.
Traces the hidden safety assumption beyond direct callers into source and executable evidence.

contexts.label: Production app launch
contexts.reason: Use this when automated checks must support an explicit staged rollout and rollback decision.

picks.reason: Automates lint, types, tests and builds with deployment feedback and previews.
Checks readiness, staged cohorts, production behavior and rollback preparation.

contexts.label: Small team PR
contexts.reason: Use this when delivery mainly needs understandable commits and a reviewable pull request with concrete proof.

picks.reason: Keeps branches short-lived and commits atomic while preserving versions and changelogs.
Writes a visual PR body with before-and-after proof and explicit merge risk.

contexts.label: Production service operations
contexts.reason: Use this when on-call questions need actionable telemetry rather than a new workflow integration.

picks.reason: Connects logs, metrics, traces and symptom alerts to on-call questions and runbooks.

contexts.label: Langfuse AI app
contexts.reason: Use this for an AI application using Langfuse that also needs broader service-health visibility.

picks.reason: Uses current docs and CLI schemas for datasets, experiments, prompts and instrumentation.
Adds service-level telemetry and exercised symptom alerts beyond AI evaluation workflows.

contexts.label: Configured Benny triage
contexts.reason: Use this only with an installed Benny pack, Cursor Automations, Slack and working tracker adapters.

picks.reason: Classifies one Slack thread and creates a ticket only for a clear, new bug.

contexts.label: Recurring agent mistakes
contexts.reason: Use this when session failures should improve the development environment rather than accumulate as instructions.

picks.reason: Identifies navigation, enforcement and tool-cost failures from sessions and current checks.
Turns repeated instructions into lint, metadata, runtime checks or scripts where possible.

contexts.label: Team change handoff
contexts.reason: Use this when teammates need both durable decision records and a paced explanation of a shipped change.

picks.reason: Preserves alternatives, consequences and public behavior using existing documentation conventions.
Explains a change through source-grounded how and why, with incremental diagrams.
